Ryzen is coming out with a total of 16 lanes for graphics. What's the theoretical difference between performance for cards running with 8x/8x vs 16x/8x or 16x/4x?

edit: I found this article. Apparently it makes no difference at all.
How many PCIe lanes really make a difference?

It's simple. 16 lanes means one graphics card x16 or two x8. 16x+8x needs 24 lanes, 16x+4x needs 20. If there aren't enough lanes, the bus will clock down. Running multiple GPUs on different clock rates is generally a bad idea because most software isn't optimized for that. Also having an 8x+8x configuration is sometimes slower as a 16x GPU because the bus is the bottleneck, not the processing power.

If the same bus is used for mass storage(like M2) or network it gets worse. IMO a decent CPU should have at least 40 lanes.
